name: Coloboma of Optic Disc

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Ophthalmologic Diagnostic Criteria for Optic Disc Coloboma

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated, excavated defect in the optic nerve head consistent with coloboma
Visual field defects corresponding to the location of the optic disc coloboma
Presence of associated ocular anomalies such as microphthalmia or iris coloboma
Confirmation of optic nerve head excavation by ocular imaging (OCT or fundus photography)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic optic disc excavation confirmed by clinical exam and imaging, with or without associated ocular anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features are present.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic disc excavation with colobomatous defect
Visual field defect corresponding to coloboma location
searchTerms: visual field missing where coloboma is
blind spot corresponding to eye defect

rare.symptomName: Syndromic systemic anomalies (e.g., CHARGE syndrome features)
rare.notes: Rarely present in isolated optic disc coloboma
searchTerms: multiple birth defects with eye and ear problems

imaging: Fundus photography showing optic disc excavation
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating colobomatous defect
Visual field testing showing corresponding defects
other: Clinical ophthalmologic examination revealing characteristic optic nerve head morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Smaller optic nerve head without excavated colobomatous defect
Diffuse optic nerve pallor rather than localized excavation
Funnel-shaped excavation with central glial tuft
History of optic nerve injury or ischemia

redFlags: Sudden vision loss or rapid deterioration
Presence of systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic association
references: Chang MY, et al. Optic nerve coloboma: clinical features and management. Surv Ophthalmol. 2018.
Orphanet: Coloboma of optic disc - ORPHA:98947
Mansour AM. Congenital optic disc anomalies. Curr Opin Ophthalmol. 2016.
